# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-13 (Extended v109)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring Year 4)**: (1) Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon; le Petit-Picpus convent district; M. Gillenormand's residences; Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens (Rue de l'Ouest side); village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; (2) English provincial harbor towns (Dunstead, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Staveford, Gulhaven); river crossing at Dungate. **Environmental conditions (Spring Year 4)**: warm air, light and shadow in Luxembourg, sky pure, sparrows chirping in chestnut-trees; rain threatening since morning but holding off; frost silvering hedges overnight; bell for vespers rings thinly; baker's boy late, line at oven grows long; smoke from chimneys lay flat; wind off water smells salt and tar; bees hum in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarrel over fish heads; road rutted and puddled after thaw.

## Primary Locations
**LUXEMBOURG GARDENS**: Fountain basin with swans; statues including Leonidas and Spartacus; "his alley" on Rue de l'Ouest side with recurring bench surrounded by aureole in narrative focus; bench by Gladiator near other end of walk. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus convent. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **GORBEAU HOVEL**: 50-52, Salpêtrière district; Marius's attic cabinet, 30 francs annually. **M. MABEUF'S COTTAGE**: Village of Austerlitz; thatched cottage, fifty crowns yearly. **ROUSSEAU'S RESTAURANT** and **CAFÉ VOLTAIRE**: Where Marius dined with Courfeyrac.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as assistant gardener in convent; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. Nuns unaware of circumstances.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. **Status (Winter Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps around Gorbeau house; confident convict nearby.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development Continued

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, now twenty years old (as of current spring Year 4); three years since left grandfather.

**Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen; believes grandfather burned it.

**Political evolution (Winter Year 3 → Spring Year 4)**: Converted to Bonapartism and republicanism; political fevers dissipated through reverie; Revolution of 1830 calmed views. No longer held firm opinions; sympathies directed to humanity over nation, woman over people, idea over deed, poet over hero. Preferred introspection to action.

**Material condition (Spring Year 4)**: Occupied Gorbeau cabinet 30 francs annually. Daily sustenance cost 20 sous (365 francs yearly); clothing 100 francs; linen/washing 100 francs. Total: 450 francs. No fireplace. Wardrobe: two black suits, three shirts. Earned approximately seven hundred francs yearly from law practice and publisher M. Magimel's work (prospectuses, translation, annotation, biography compilation). **Refused advancement (Winter Year 3)**: M. Magimel offered lodging, regular occupation, fifteen hundred francs yearly—Marius refused to preserve liberty and dignity. After securing living with certainty, deliberately stopped working to dedicate time to thought and meditation.

**Philosophy and character**: Brain absorbed slowly in wisdom or folly, resulting in passivity resembling philosophy. Real character revealed through aspirations and dreams more surely than deliberate ideas. Each dreams according to nature.

**Pleasures and habits (Winter Year 3)**: Long solitary walks on outer boulevards, Champs-de-Mars, Luxembourg's least frequented alleys. Spent half-days observing market gardens. Attended occasional evening parties at generals' homes.

**Grandfather quarrel**: Violent quarrel three years ago; remained estranged without rapprochement—"Marius was the brass vase, while Father Gillenormand was the iron pot." Grandfather's suffering locked within breast.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C**: Met Courfeyrac at Place Saint-Michel; became good friends. Courfeyrac introduced him to Café Musain. Did not enter decidedly into group but remained cordial. Close to **M. Mabeuf**—owed him revolution within soul; indebted for knowing and loving his father. **Recent social activities (Spring Year 4)**: Dined with Courfeyrac at Rousseau's (six francs), ate like ogre, gave waiter six sous; discussed newspapers and Audry de Puyraveau's discourse. Breakfasted at Café Voltaire with Courfeyrac and circle of students; discussed Sorbonne absurdities and Guicherat's dictionaries; exclaimed "But it is very agreeable, all the same to have the cross!"

## The Mysterious Couple at Luxembourg and Marius's Awakening (Current Focus)

**Initial six-month observation (over one year prior)**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty years old and very young girl (thirteen/fourteen) seated daily on bench, Rue de l'Ouest side. Man: retired military officer, robust, weary, kindly but unapproachable; wore blue trousers, blue frock coat, broad-brimmed hat (always new), black cravat, white quaker shirt, white hair. Girl: thin, almost homely, awkward, insignificant, with promise of handsome eyes; wore badly cut black merino gown (convent scholar dress). **Named M. Leblanc and "his daughter" by narrative.**

**Six-month interruption**: Observation ceased for unknown reason.

**Reunion and girl's transformation (Summer Year 3)**: Marius returned to Luxembourg on serene morning. At first thought she was another daughter; on second examination recognized her as same girl. **In six months little girl had become young maiden—rare phenomenon when girls blossom suddenly.** No longer school-girl in felt hat and scholar shoes; became well-dressed person. Wore dress of black damask, cape of same material, bonnet of white crape, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe. Whole toilette exhaled youthful penetrating perfume.

**Marius's indifference (Summer Year 3)**: When she raised eyelids, Marius approached but found in her veiled azure only child's glance. She looked at him indifferently. Marius continued promenade, thought about something else. Paid no further attention; passed near bench habitually; thought no more about girl now beautiful than when homely.

**First meaningful glance and awakening (Spring Year 4—Chapter 13)**: On warm day, Luxembourg inundated with light and shade. As Marius passed near the bench, the young girl raised her eyes to him. **Their glances met.** Narrative reflection: That first gaze of a soul which does not yet know itself is like dawn in sky—awakening of something radiant and strange. Dangerous charm of unexpected gleam composed of all innocence of present and all passion of future. Virgin maiden sets snare unknown to herself, capturing hearts without wishing or knowing.

**Marius's emotional transformation (Spring Year 4)**: That evening perceived for first time he had worn everyday clothes. Resolved to dress differently. Buttoned coat to top, examined trousers. Marched on bench yet movements purely mechanical; mind occupied with schoolwork and tragedies. As he drew near, pace slackened; he halted and retraced steps. Could not explain himself. For first time in fifteen months, reflected that gentleman had likely noticed his assiduity and considered it singular. Following day wore new coat again. Seated himself midway on bench surveying white bonnet and black dress. Left only when gates closed.

**State of mind (Spring Year 4)**: Isolation, detachment, pride, independence, taste of nature, absence of daily material activity, life within himself, secret conflicts of chastity, benevolent ecstasy towards all creation had prepared Marius for possession called passion. His worship of his father had gradually become religion, retreated to depths of soul. Something was required in foreground. Love came. Brain felt on fire. She appeared more beautiful than ever—wholly feminine and angelic. Seemed to him floating free in azure heavens. Horribly vexed because there was dust on his boots. Followed her with eyes until she disappeared. Walked about Luxembourg garden like madman, possibly laughed aloud and talked to himself. Dreamy near children's nurses; each thought him in love with her.

**Behavioral escalation (Spring Year 4)**: Ate like ogre with Courfeyrac; gave waiter six sous; spoke excitedly about newspapers and discourse; breakfasted and ate even more than evening before; very thoughtful and very merry; laughed uproariously; tenderly embraced men presented to him; interrupted discussions to exclaim about the cross.

**Strategic approach (Spring Year 4)**: Had finally grown bold and approached bench. Did not pass in front of it in obedience to instinct of timidity and prudence common to lovers. Considered it better not to attract "attention of the father." Combined stations behind trees and pedestals of statues with profound diplomacy, so might be seen as much as possible by young girl and as little as possible by old gentleman. Sometimes remained motionless by half-hour together in shade of Leonidas or Spartacus, holding book, eyes gently raised seeking beautiful girl. She turned charming profile towards him with vague smile. While conversing naturally with white-haired man, bent upon Marius all reveries of virginal and passionate eye. Ancient manœuvre which Eve understood first day of world, every woman from first day of her life—her mouth replied to one, glance replied to another.

**M. Leblanc's response (Spring Year 4)**: Finally noticed something. Often when Marius arrived, rose and began walking. Abandoned accustomed place and adopted bench by Gladiator near other end of walk, as though to see whether Marius would pursue them thither. Marius did not understand and committed error. Began to grow inexact, no longer brought daughter every day. Sometimes came alone. Then Marius did not stay. Another blunder.

**Escalation of passion (Spring Year 4)**: From phase of timidity, had passed by natural and fatal progress to phase of blindness. Love increased. Dreamed of it every night. Unexpected bliss happened: found handkerchief on bench M. Leblanc and daughter had just quitted. Very simple, without embroidery, white, fine, exhaled ineffable perfume. Seized it with rapture. Marked with letters U. F. Marius knew nothing of beautiful child—neither family name, Christian name nor abode; these two letters were first thing of her he had gained possession of, adorable initials upon which immediately began constructing scaffolding. U was evidently Christian name. "Ursule!" he thought, "what a delicious name!" Kissed handkerchief, drank it in, placed it on heart, on flesh during day; at night laid it beneath lips to fall asleep on it.

**Recent distress (Spring Year 4)**: Once "his Ursule" caused him very serious grief. One day when she persuaded M. Leblanc to leave bench and stroll along walk. Brisk May breeze swaying crests of plaintain-trees. Father and daughter arm in arm had just passed Marius's bench. Marius had risen to his feet behind them, following them with eyes, as was fitting in desperate situation of his soul.

## M. Mabeuf

**Character**: Ecclesiastic, botanist, editor, man of books and flowers.

**Servant—Mother Plutarque (Spring Year 4)**: Innocent spinster; cat Sultan filled her heart; glory consisted in white caps; could read. Mother Plutarque fell asleep in chair before fire caught.

**New residence (Winter Year 3)**: Relocated to village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; established in thatched cottage for fifty crowns yearly with three rooms and garden enclosed by hedge with well. Carried _Flora_, copper-plates, herbariums, portfolios, books. On entrance night: "We have the indigo!"

**Philosophical disposition**: Brain absorbed slowly in wisdom or folly; results in passivity resembling philosophy. Habits swung like pendulum.

## Friends of the A B C (Revolutionary Organization)

**Identity and purpose**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—_Abaissé_, the debased (the people). Wished to elevate people. Secret society in embryonic state, not numerous.

**Meetings (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: Back room Café Musain; argand lamp lighted. Nearly all haranguing; tossed words, caught up in turn. Peaceable tumults.

**Members**: Enjolras (believer, sober), Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students; cordial with working classes.

## English Provincial Towns

**Population movements**: Yera Haskick (Dunstead → Kelmere); Rinelle (Kelford → Torton); Kadrek Brackick (followed to Torton). **Births**: Ferald and Isvie Stenworth (son/daughter, Dunstead, parents Luwyn Brackick); Zavus Prydenridge (son, Ostcombe, parents Wenelle and Rovus).

**Activities and observations (Winter/Spring Year 4)**: Isric Thornmere mended torn sleeve by window, spoke little; asked Wenelle "Will it rain?"—she shrugged. Rozek Stenenridge told Luena "You look tired." Yera Haskick laughed alone. Vesmira Thornmere and Wenelle Lindmere discussed weather, harvest, lame horse. Taric Corrley complained aching back; walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Kadan bought ribbon then regretted. Lurald Stenworth argued with carter over sack of oats price. Peten Haskick said "salt price a scandal"—Ulrald agreed. Ulrald Corrford counted coins twice, came up penny short. Yewyn Corrford fell asleep before fire caught. Rorald Lindmere gave Gadan Corrley solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Ravenmere. **Ferald Stenworth** mended torn sleeve by window, said little. **Luena Stenenridge** won copper chalice from Rozek Stenenridge at cards, fairly, and kept it. **Fenelle Lindmere** confided to Luwyn Brackick that Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family (claim).

**Earlier claims and rumors (prior)**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (claim). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body). Granary fire set on purpose (rumor). Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing mill ledger rewritten. Kassa Brackick confided to Yewyn Corrford mill ledger rewritten.

## Winter Year 3 Events (Paris)

**Student assembly**: Students of law and medicine summoned to Place du Panthéon at midday to deliberate on artillery of National Guard—conflict between Minister of War and citizen's militia over cannon at Louvre courtyard.

**M. Gillenormand's rage**: Read announcement in Royalist sheet; flew into rage; denounced students as pack of brats, Republicans as one nose and handkerchief with galley-slaves. Called progress madness, humanity dream, revolution crime, republic monster.

**New scheming (Winter Year 3)**: Aunt Gillenormand plotted to have Lieutenant Théodule (nephew, lancer regiment) take Marius's place in grandfather's affections.
